items.title: Give every execFileSync blob and tree read in done-prepare-generated-metadata an explicit maxBuffer
items.context: isolatedBlobHash reads a staged blob with execFileSync and no maxBuffer, so Node's 1 MiB default applies and a larger blob throws ENOBUFS. Audit the whole module for sibling helpers reading blob or tree content the same way - isolatedGit and treeBlobHash are the likely candidates - and give each an explicit generous maxBuffer rather than fixing only the one observed to fail.

happy.desc: In a temp git repo, stage a 1,400,000-byte file as a managed metadata path, supply its sha256 in verifiedHashes, call commitImmutableMetadataTree -> result.ok is true with a valid commitSha; WHY: exercises both isolatedBlobHash (index verification) and treeBlobHash (tree verification) with content above the old 1 MiB Node default, matching the measured artifact size from B-9ff1

edge.desc: Same temp-repo setup with a file of exactly 1,048,577 bytes -> commit path returns ok:true; WHY: one byte past the old Node maxBuffer default (1,048,576), the smallest size that triggered ENOBUFS before the fix

adversarial.desc: grep each of the three function bodies -- isolatedBlobHash, isolatedGit, treeBlobHash -- in done-prepare-generated-metadata.ts and confirm each execFileSync call includes a maxBuffer option; WHY: a partial fix that patches only isolatedBlobHash (the observed failure) leaves the identical latent limit on the other two helpers

The maxBuffer value is at least an order of magnitude above the old 1 MiB default (at least 10 MiB); WHY: the artifact grows linearly with validate command count and was already 1.3 MiB at 100 commands, so a ceiling barely above 1 MiB recreates the same cliff at a slightly higher command count

items.userSees: The metadata commit succeeds for a story whose test-evidence.json exceeds one mebibyte, where it previously failed with verified metadata changed after manifest verification

items.title: Stop the catch from turning an unreadable blob into a silent digest mismatch and surface the real cause
items.context: The catch currently returns null, which the caller compares against the expected digest and reports as verified metadata changed after manifest verification. Distinguish blob genuinely absent from blob could not be read, keep the fail-closed posture, and make the surfaced reason name the underlying error so the next person does not spend hours attributing it to concurrency.

happy.desc: When a staged blob IS readable, isolatedBlobHash and treeBlobHash return its correct sha256 hash and the commit path succeeds; WHY: the error-handling fix must not break the normal read-and-hash path

When a blob read fails (simulated ENOBUFS or equivalent), the commit-path failure reason names the underlying error cause (buffer overflow, error code, or OS message), not the generic string verified metadata changed after manifest verification; WHY: surfacing the real cause is the diagnosability fix that turns the next occurrence from hours of misattribution into minutes

edge.desc: When execFileSync throws an error other than blob-not-found (e.g. ENOBUFS, EPERM, or a git crash), the surfaced reason includes the original error message or code from the child process; WHY: the current catch discards ALL error information and the fix must preserve it for the operator

adversarial.desc: An unreadable blob (execFileSync throws any error) never compares equal to any expected hash value -- the commit path always fails closed with a diagnostic message; WHY: if the fix changes the sentinel from null to some value that could accidentally match an expected hash, it opens a fail-open path where corrupted reads are silently accepted

The error message for an infrastructure failure (ENOBUFS, EPERM) is textually distinct from the error message for a blob that is genuinely absent from the index; WHY: conflating infrastructure failures with missing-blob is exactly the original defect -- if the fix treats both as the same generic error, the diagnosability improvement is cosmetic

items.userSees: When a blob read fails during the metadata commit, the reported reason names the actual cause such as a buffer length being exceeded while reading a staged blob, instead of the misleading verified metadata changed after manifest verification

items.title: Add a committed regression test that stages a file larger than one mebibyte and asserts the commit path still succeeds
items.context: The regression must fail on the pre-fix tree. Stage a blob above 1048576 bytes, drive the same commit path, and assert success; a fixture below the limit proves nothing because that is exactly the size at which the defect is invisible.

happy.desc: A committed test file exists that stages a blob larger than 1,048,576 bytes in a temp repo, drives the commitImmutableMetadataTree path, and asserts result.ok === true with a valid commitSha; WHY: the regression test exercises the exact failure class -- a large blob through the isolated commit path

edge.desc: The fixture blob is generated at a size strictly above 1,048,576 bytes, not at 1,000,000 or any round number below the Node maxBuffer default; WHY: a fixture below the limit passes on the UNFIXED tree and proves nothing -- this is exactly why the defect survived undetected

adversarial.desc: The regression test fails when run without the maxBuffer fix (demonstrated by running against the pre-fix tree or by temporarily reverting the maxBuffer additions in isolatedBlobHash and treeBlobHash); WHY: a test that passes on both the fixed and unfixed tree is a tautology, not a regression test -- the plan explicitly requires RED-before-GREEN evidence

The fixture blob is a deterministic byte sequence whose on-disk size cannot be reduced below 1,048,576 by any gitattributes filter, delta compression, or encoding normalization; WHY: if the fixture content can be shrunk by any transform in the pipeline, the test silently stops exercising the failure path

items.userSees: The committed regression that stages a file above the one-mebibyte boundary and exercises the isolated commit path reports PASS

items.title: Bound the aggregate evidence artifact or commit a rationale naming the change that will, and ship whichever the decision is
items.context: Per-command output is already truncated to twelve thousand characters by trimOutput in core/validation-executor.ts, so the unbounded dimension is the NUMBER of configured commands serialised into test-evidence.json by handlers/verifier.ts. Raising maxBuffer moves the cliff; it does not remove it. This item requires a BINDING outcome, not an evaluation: either the bounding ships in this story, or a committed rationale records why unbounded growth is acceptable and names the change that will address it. Closing this item with a written opinion and no shipped consequence is exactly the unexamined growth cliff this story exists to end.

happy.desc: Exactly one of two shipped outcomes exists: (A) a code change in the serialization path (persistStoryValidationEvidence or writeTestEvidence) that bounds the aggregate artifact size, or (B) a committed rationale document at a discoverable path that names a concrete successor story ID or issue reference for bounding aggregate growth; WHY: the item requires a BINDING disposition, not an evaluation

edge.desc: If outcome A (bounding ships): serializing command results whose total would exceed the bound produces a bounded artifact with a visible truncation marker or a diagnostic cap, not a crash or silent data loss; WHY: a declared bound that is not enforced is not a shipped outcome

If outcome B (deferred with rationale): the rationale is a committed file in the repository (not a PR comment, plan paragraph, or commit message) and the named successor is a real story ID, issue number, or tracked backlog item that can be looked up; WHY: a rationale embedded in existing narrative has no binding force and no discoverable successor

adversarial.desc: The item is NOT closed with only a prose paragraph in plan.md, background.md, a commit message, or a code comment explaining why growth is acceptable -- the disposition must be either shipped code in the serialization path OR a standalone committed rationale document; WHY: the third outcome (opinion with no shipped consequence) is exactly the unexamined growth cliff this story exists to end

If outcome A: the bound does not silently discard evidence entries -- it either truncates individual command outputs with a visible marker, caps the number of serialized entries with a diagnostic count, or errors with a message naming the measured size and the limit; WHY: silent evidence loss is a new class of the same silent-failure defect this story exists to fix

items.title: Emit a visible advisory as the evidence artifact approaches the buffer limit so the cliff is marked and not merely moved
items.context: After the maxBuffer raise and the diagnosability repair an operator still gets zero advance notice before hitting the wall. The repository already carries a threshold-classification model - buildLedgerSizing in core/proofstory.ts classifies capacity and warns before hard failure - and the same shape applies here: when the serialised evidence artifact passes a warning fraction of the limit, validate should print an advisory naming the measured size and the limit. Without it the next person who adds validate commands meets the same silent wall at a higher number.

happy.desc: An artifact below the warning fraction produces no advisory

edge.desc: An artifact above the warning fraction prints an advisory naming the measured size and the limit

adversarial.desc: The advisory is emitted without changing the pass or fail verdict of validate
